official.deadline_note: Two application rounds are published: round one closes Sunday 28 February 2027 (outcomes by 2 April 2027, applications stay under consideration until all awards are allocated), round two closes Sunday 16 May 2027 (all outcomes by 11 June 2027). The scholarships directory listing carries 28 February 2027 as the final deadline.
official.application_cycle: 2027/28 cycle, for taught Masters courses starting September 2027
official.status_note: Applications for Masters degrees for 2027/28 opened on 1 October 2026. The scholarship form is not published openly: offer holders are notified by email with details of how to apply once the form is available, and the scholarship can only be applied for after a conditional or unconditional offer is held.
official.tuition_coverage_note: This scholarship is paid as a fee reduction for your first year of study only and can only be used as a fee reduction. It cannot be used towards other costs, including but not exclusive to maintenance or accommodation costs.
official.funding_period: one-off tuition fee discount on first year of study
benefits: Can be combined with the Masters International Regional Scholarship or external funding as long as total support does not exceed 100% of tuition fees
May also be combinable with a School or Faculty scholarship (check the other scheme's terms)
eligibility: Be classified as an international student for fee purposes
Hold a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time taught Masters course starting in September 2027
Demonstrate an excellent academic track record and be predicted to achieve or have achieved a minimum of a Bachelor's degree with a 2:1 (hons) or equivalent
Show excellent professional and personal skills evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities
requirements: Scholarship application form submitted after receiving a conditional or unconditional offer; offer holders are notified by email when the form is available
A separate scholarship application is required for each course if you hold offers for multiple courses
Demonstrate excellent professional and personal skills evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities
documents: Official degree certificate and transcripts showing degree class/grade and grades in each module (interim transcript if still studying), with a grading scale where the transcript does not make the class clear
Evidence of English language proficiency, if held at the time of application

Course-dependent documents as published for Masters applications: a CV, references or contact details for two referees, evidence of professional qualifications, a portfolio, or a personal statement no longer than one A4 page
selection_criteria: High academic achievement (2:1 hons equivalent or better, predicted or achieved)
Excellent professional and personal skills evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities
The final scholarship awarded is determined by the University and all decisions are final
coverage: Partial tuition fee reduction of £3,000, £6,000 or £16,000, applied to the first year of study only
Cannot be used towards maintenance or accommodation costs
application_method: Apply for the Masters course through the University of Leeds applicant portal (2027/28 applications opened 1 October 2026)
Once a conditional or unconditional offer is held, wait for the University email with scholarship application details and submit the scholarship form
Submit a separate scholarship application for each course you hold an offer for

If applying for a scholarship, ensure the course application is submitted at least one month before the scholarship deadline and indicate the scholarship deadline in the funding section of the application form
official.application_route: Course application through the University's applicant portal first, then a separate scholarship application once you hold an offer (details emailed to offer holders).
official.citizenship_residency: Must be classified as an international student for fee purposes; no other nationality or residency rule is published on the scholarship page.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The scholarship is restricted to applicants classified as international for fee purposes, so UK fee-status students are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to eligible full-time taught Masters courses only. Excluded: the MBA (which runs its own MBA Excellence Scholarship scheme) and all fully online courses.
official.duration: Award applies to the first year of study only; it is a one-off fee reduction and cannot be deferred to a later year.
official.description: The University of Leeds offers a substantial number of scholarships worth £3,000, £6,000 or £16,000 to support eligible international students applying to taught Masters degrees starting in September 2027. The awards recognise and reward high academic achievement and are paid as a tuition fee reduction on the first year of study only.
official.region: Europe (United Kingdom); open to international fee-status applicants worldwide
official.program_type: University merit scholarship (taught Masters tuition fee discount)
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page sets no separate English test requirement. The University's published minimum for Masters degrees is IELTS Academic or IELTS for UKVI (Academic) 6.5 overall with no less than 6.0 in each component; TOEFL iBT 88 overall with no less than 20 reading, 19 listening, 22 speaking and 21 writing (tests before 21 January 2026) or 4.5 overall (tests on or after 21 January 2026); PTE Academic or PTE Academic UKVI 64 overall with no less than 60 in each component. Some courses set higher requirements.

not_confirmed: The scholarship page publishes no document checklist specific to the scholarship application form itself
No living cost, travel, installation or maintenance support is offered; the award is tuition-only
verification.notes: Award values, tiering, eligibility, excluded courses, terms and both deadline rounds were confirmed on the University of Leeds scholarship page; the English requirement and application/document process were taken from the University's official entry requirements and Masters application pages, all on leeds.ac.uk.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a partial tuition discount, not a full ride: at best it removes £16,000 from your first-year international tuition bill while you still fund living costs, accommodation, insurance and travel yourself. You cannot apply until you already hold a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time taught Masters starting September 2027, so the date that really matters is the course application deadline - Leeds advises scholarship-seekers to apply for the course at least one month before the scholarship deadline. If you hold offers for several courses you must file a separate scholarship form for each one, and the MBA plus every fully online course is excluded outright.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded or partially funded international applicants with a 2:1-equivalent degree and a strong work or extracurricular record who already hold an offer on a full-time taught Masters at Leeds.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for your course as early as possible through the applicant portal (2027/28 applications opened 1 October 2026) and enter your scholarship deadline in the funding section so admissions can prioritise the decision
Confirm on Course Search that your chosen course is not the MBA or a fully online course before investing time in a scholarship application
Watch the inbox linked to your applicant portal (including spam folders) after your offer arrives, because the scholarship form link is emailed to offer holders rather than published openly
Gather evidence of work experience and extracurricular achievements up front, since these are explicitly assessed alongside your academic record
Line up transcripts with module grades and a grading scale, plus an English test result less than two years old at course start
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the scholarship before holding an offer - the form is only available once you have a conditional or unconditional offer
Assuming the discount covers living costs - it cannot be used for maintenance or accommodation, which can leave the UK student visa financial requirement unmet
Holding an offer for an excluded course (MBA or fully online programme)
Treating the award as flexible - it cannot be deferred to the following year or transferred to another Leeds course
Applying through an International Partner Agreement while expecting to stack multiple Leeds scholarships - only the single highest-value award may be accepted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except part of first-year tuition: living costs, accommodation, flights and travel to the UK, visa fees and immigration health surcharge, and the tuition for any second year of study.
document_audit: Interim transcripts must show module-level grades plus a grading scale if your transcript does not make the degree class obvious
The scholarship page names no scholarship-specific documents, so expect the form to draw on what you already submitted with your course application - inconsistencies between the two will surface
All documents must be in English or accompanied by certified translations
alerts: The directory lists 28 February 2027 as the final deadline, but the page also advertises a second round closing 16 May 2027 - treat February as the working target, since round-one applicants hear by 2 April and unsuccessful round-one applicants are reconsidered in later rounds
A course application submitted less than a month before the scholarship deadline risks a decision arriving too late to enter the round
Leeds does not permit deferrals, so a 2027-entry award cannot be carried into 2028 if your plans slip
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for the course through the University's applicant portal, receive a decision (Leeds aims for ten working days when documents are complete), then complete the separate scholarship form emailed to offer holders before the round deadline.
